Unexpected Ring-Opening of Benzocyclobutenes upon Reaction with Lithium in Tetrahydrofuran
By Adalbert Maercker\*, Willi Berkulin, and Peter Schiess
Although the conrotatory ring-opening of the benzocyclobutene radical anion is thermally allowed, previously reported results were revoked shortly after their publication $^{[1]}$ .

We have found a completely different reaction path—scission of a $C_{aryl}-CH_{2}$ bond—in the reaction of benzocyclobutene (1,2-dihydrocyclobutabenzene) $^{[**]}$ 1 $^{[2]}$ with lithium powder in tetrahydrofuran (THF). The expected o-xylene was not detected, even in trace amounts. Instead, after hydrolysis ethylbenzene 9 and its subsequent product 8, which may have been formed via the dilithio compound 6, was obtained (Scheme 1; the relative yields were determined by gas chromatography: after four weeks at room temperature conversion was only 20%).
